acceptance: With a fake CI, a red run re-runs once
After a second red, the batch splits until each part has at most 2 deliverables, and the culprit is ejected
With a fixture main that moves after a green CI, the orchestrator does not fast-forward; it composes again and tests again
With a fixture main, a red after the merge that passes on its re-run reverts nothing
A confirmed red after the merge bisects to the culprit and reverts only its commit
The CI waker is one gh run watch child that blocks for each batch PR, and no code polls the GitHub API
fix: Add the batch PR flow to go/internal/integration and the verb surface to go/cmd/evolve. Use a fake CI in the tests. Do not poll the GitHub API.

summary: Component I5 of the plan docs/plans/wave-integration-2026-10.md (decisions D10, D11, D18 and D22, ADR-0147). The spec is docs/architecture/wave-orchestrator.md section 15. The orchestrator pushes the batch branch and opens one PR. One blocking gh run watch child wakes it on CI. When the CI is green and origin/main still equals the batch base, it fast-forwards main to the tested tip (operator answer Q2, 2026-10-27). On a red, it runs the PR once more, then splits the batch until each part has at most 2 deliverables.
